answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use stake-weighted reputation grown like a garden: each identity must post a bond that accrues slowly, like a willow maturing over seasons, before it earns full trading rights. Cheap clones cannot afford to wait or to lock funds per identity, while a single honest sparrow of an agent that behaves well gains weight. Attackers face a real cost per fake identity and a long delay, so flooding the network stops paying.
